title: observation: the cross-org identity refresh does not re-arm between two organization switches with no session read in between
body:
Found while measuring #5719 (see PR #5749). Filed separately because it is a different failure
mode from the one that card described, and because its **reachability is unproven** — what is
measured below is a deterministic client-side fact, not a demonstrated user-visible harm.

## Background — how identity re-resolves across an org switch today

`AuthProvider.switchOrganization` never calls `loadSession()`. Identity nonetheless re-resolves,
through the objectui#4467 rotation subscription, because of a **token-spelling asymmetry**:

- `createAuthClient.getSession()` stores `payload.session.token` — the **unsigned** value
  (`sys_session.token`).
- `createBearerFetch` stores whatever arrives in `set-auth-token` — the **signed**
  `token.signature` value, which better-auth's `bearer()` emits for any response that stages a
  session `Set-Cookie`, and `POST /organization/set-active` always stages one.

Two spellings of one session, so an org switch flips storage unsigned to signed. `TokenStorage.set`
notifies on a value change, that reads as a rotation, and `loadSession()` runs. The follow-up
`get-session` re-stores the unsigned form, which **re-arms** the mechanism for the next switch.
Measured against better-auth 1.6.28 in #5749.

## The observation

The re-arm is the load-bearing step, and it costs a network round trip. Two `set-active`
responses with no `get-session` in between carry the **same** signed value — same session, same
deterministic HMAC — so the second one is a no-op write and produces no rotation at all:

```
TokenStorage.set(unsigned)   // steady state after mount
TokenStorage.set(signed)     // switch 1  -> rotation fires (1)
TokenStorage.set(signed)     // switch 2  -> NO rotation    (still 1)
```

Measured directly (probe run against `packages/auth`, not landed): rotations after switch 1 = 1,
after switch 2 = 1. With an intervening `TokenStorage.set(unsigned)` standing in for the
follow-up `get-session`, the count goes to 3 — i.e. the mechanism does re-arm, but only once
that read lands.

`AuthProvider`'s `sessionLoadInFlight` guard is a second, independent suppressor on the same
window: a rotation observed while a `loadSession()` is in flight is deliberately dropped.

## What is NOT claimed

- **No server-side authorization impact.** The server re-derives from the session on every
  request. Anything here is client-side gating only, the same class as #5619 and #5719.
- **Not shown to be user-reachable.** Whether a person can switch organizations twice inside one
  `get-session` round trip, and whether the resulting frame is one they can act in, was not
  measured. It may well be unreachable in practice.
- The consequence, *if* reachable, would be the over-permissive direction #5719 described:
  `user.positions` left on an earlier organization's answer while `useWorkspaceAdminStatus`
  reports `isAdmin: true, isResolved: true`, because that hook short-circuits on any positive leg.

## Suggested next step

Decide whether the console should stop depending on an undeclared spelling accident for
cross-org identity, rather than patching this window specifically. The obvious candidate — an
explicit `refreshSession()` in `switchOrganization` — was deliberately **not** taken in #5749
because the rotation path already spends exactly one `get-session` per switch, so it would
double-fetch on the common path. A cheaper shape may exist (for example, re-resolving only when
the switch actually changed the active organization), but that is a design call, not a fix to
make in passing.

PR #5749 pins the mechanism that currently provides the guarantee, so any change to it is at
least visible.
